post.x-zenesis-title: Create Import Job for a New Table
post.summary: Create Import Job for a New Table
post.description:
Create an import job to import data into a new table asynchronously. Max allowed file size is 100 MB.

Workflow of Asynchronous Import API:

1. Create Import Job:
   - Initiate the import by calling the Create Import Job API.
   - A unique JOBID will be returned in the response, which serves as the reference for tracking the import job.

2. Check Job Status:
   - Use the Get Import Job Details API to monitor the status of the import job.
   - The JOBID must be used in the request to check the status periodically (e.g., every 10 seconds).
   - The response will include a JOBCODE, which indicates the current state of the job.

Handling Import Job Status Based on JOBCODE:
  - If the JOBCODE is 1001 or 1002, wait for a few seconds and repeat the status check loop.
  - If the JOBCODE is 1003, stop the status check and inspect the error message for details.
  - If the JOBCODE is 1005, verify the validity of the JOBID and terminate the status check.
  - If the JOBCODE is 1004, the job is complete, and the import summary will be returned.

Limitations:
  - The import job summary is retained only for one hour after job completion.
  - A maximum of 5 simultaneous import jobs is allowed per organization.
  - A maximum file size of 100 MB can be imported.

get.x-zenesis-title: Create Export Job using SQL Query
get.summary: Create Export Job using SQL Query
get.description:
Create an export job using an SQL SELECT statement to initiate data export asynchronously.

Workflow:
1. Create Export Job:
  - Call the Create Export Job API.
  - Receive a unique JOBID to track the export status.

2. Check Export Job Status:
  - Use the JOBID with the Get Export Job Details API.
  - Poll every few seconds to get the current JOBCODE.

   JOBCODEs and Meaning:
   - 1001: JOB NOT INITIATED
     → Export job acknowledged but not started. Retry after a short delay.
   - 1002: JOB IN PROGRESS
     → Export is currently being processed. Continue polling.
   - 1003: ERROR OCCURRED
     → An error occurred. Stop polling and investigate the error.
   - 1004: JOB COMPLETED
     → Export process completed. Proceed to download.
   - 1005: JOB NOT FOUND
     → Provided JOBID is invalid. Stop polling and verify the JOBID.

3. Download Exported Data:
  - Once JOBCODE is 1004, use the Download Exported Data API to download the exported file.

Limitations:
- Exported file will be available only for 1 hour after job completion.
- Maximum 5 concurrent export jobs are allowed per organization.

post.x-zenesis-title: Batch Import Data into New Table
post.summary: Batch Import Data into New Table
post.description:
Initiate an import job to create a new table and import data in batches into the created table.

 The Batch Import API allows you to upload large amounts of data in batches. A large data file is split into small batches, each batch not exceeding 100 MB, and imported using batch import. Alternatively, you can also use Zoho Analytics SDKs to simplify the batching process.

To import large amounts of data using Batch Import, follow the steps below:

- Split the large CSV file into batches (each batch not exceeding 100MB) and upload the first batch using the Batch Import API's {"batchKey":"start"} attribute.
- The server will generate a unique job ID and batch key for the import job and send them to the user in the response.
- Use the received batch key to submit the subsequent batches to the Batch Import API.
- Mark the end of the upload by adding {"isLastBatch":true} to the final batch.

You can check the import job status using the 'Get Import Job Details' API with the jobId received in the response.

Notes:
- After the first batch is imported, scheduled import of the remaining batches begins automatically.
- For 'Append' and 'UpdateAdd' import types, each batch is committed individually.
- For 'TruncateAdd', data is committed only after the final batch is uploaded.
- Batch order is preserved throughout.
- An import summary is stored upon job completion or failure.

requestBody.description: Sent as multipart/form-data. CONFIG is mandatory and must be sent as a form field along with FILE.

FILE.description: The batch file to be imported. Format should be multipart/form-data. Maximum allowed size per batch is 100 MB.

firstBatch.summary: Opens the batch import job. batchKey must be "start"; the response returns the batchKey to use for every following batch.

followUpBatch.summary: Uploads an intermediate batch using the batchKey returned by the first call.

lastBatch.summary: Uploads the final batch and closes the job. isLastBatch must be true.

Note:
The CSV specific attributes - commentChar, delimiter and quoted - are mandatory if autoIdentify is set to false.

Check the status of the specified import job periodically. Upon job completion the system notifies the user in the callback URL, if one was provided in the import job's CONFIG.

Job codes returned in the response:
  - 1001 - JOB NOT INITIATED: wait for a few seconds and repeat the status check.
  - 1002 - JOB IN PROGRESS: wait for a few seconds and repeat the status check.

showHiddenCols.description: Controls whether the columns that have been hidden in the view have to be exported. Defaults to true for csv, json, xml, xls and pdf, and to false for html. A column named explicitly in selectedColumns is exported even when this is false.

showPersonalCols.description: Controls whether the columns that have been marked as personal data have to be exported. Honoured only for an Account Admin, an Organization Admin or a Workspace Admin; for any other user the attribute is ignored and personal data columns are included.

includeRowNums.description: Prefixes every exported record with a sequential "Row Number" value.

validateSystemTags.description:

SyncDataConfig.title: SyncDataConfig
SyncDataConfig.description: JSONObject with configuration to initiate a data sync for the specified datasource.

userName.description: Credential of the source system - username. Required only for sources that ask for credentials at fetch time, such as FTP/SFTP hosted workbooks and MS Access sources; ignored by every other source type.

password.description: Credential of the source system - password. Required only for sources that ask for credentials at fetch time, such as FTP/SFTP hosted workbooks and MS Access sources; ignored by every other source type.

syncIntervalId.description: Targets one sync interval of the datasource. Mandatory when the datasource has more than one sync interval, otherwise the request fails with 8182. Omit for a single-interval datasource. Read the available values from dataSources[].syncIntervals[].syncIntervalId in the Get Datasources response.

RefetchDataConfig.title: RefetchDataConfig
RefetchDataConfig.description: JSONObject with the datasource credentials used to refetch data for the specified view.

isFullFetch.description:
Selects the fetch mode for database backed tables - cloud and local databases, OData feeds, local files, Analytics workspace tables, Elasticsearch and data lake tables.

- **false** - Fetches only the data changed since the last pull.
- **true** - Re-reads the source completely.

Ignored by file, web, connector and snapshot sources, which always fetch in full. Note that an incremental fetch does not remove rows that were deleted at the source.

userName.description: Credential of the source system - username. Required only for FTP/SFTP and web hosted files whose credentials are not stored with the source.

password.description: Credential of the source system - password. Required only for FTP/SFTP and web hosted files whose credentials are not stored with the source.

DatasourceConnectionConfig.title: DatasourceConnectionConfig
DatasourceConnectionConfig.description: JSONObject with the connection details of the specified datasource. This is a full replace, not a patch - attributes that are omitted are reset to their defaults rather than preserved, so resend the complete connection definition. Applies only to database style datasources.

serviceName.description: Name of the cloud service hosting the database. Matched case-insensitively.

databaseType.description: Type of the database engine. Mandatory whenever the chosen serviceName supports more than one engine, otherwise the request fails with 8079. A serviceName / databaseType combination that does not exist fails with 18055. Matched case-insensitively.

hostName.description:
The service endpoint or hostname used to identify the cloud database instance. This can be obtained from the management console provided by the respective cloud database service.

- **AMAZON ATHENA** - Provide the AWS Region value.
- **SNOWFLAKE** - Provide the full name of your account as in Snowflake.
- **All other services** - Provide the service endpoint or hostname.

cloudDatabaseName.description: The database name as in the cloud service.

instanceName.description: For the SQLSERVER database type, the instance name on which your database is present. If not specified, the default instance is used to establish the connection.

schemaName.description: Schema to connect to within the database.

s3OutputLocation.description: For the AMAZON ATHENA service, the Amazon S3 location path where the query results are stored. This path should be prefixed by s3://.

warehouseName.description: For the SNOWFLAKE service, the warehouse name on which your Snowflake database instance is present. Make sure the warehouse is active and the given user has permission to access the database.

sId.description: For the ORACLE service, the Oracle service name value.

projectId.description: For the GOOGLE BIG QUERY service, the project ID of your BigQuery project. This can be obtained from the dashboard of your Google Cloud console.

catalogName.description: Catalog to connect to. For the DATABRICKS database type the engine's default catalog is used when this is omitted.

httpPath.description: For the DATABRICKS database type, the HTTP path of the SQL warehouse or cluster.

workgroupName.description: Workgroup name. Applicable to AMAZON ATHENA and Amazon Redshift Serverless.

dataLocation.description: Region or data location. Applicable to AMAZON ATHENA and GOOGLE BIG QUERY.

connectionString.description: Full connection string. Honoured only for MongoDB database types and for the ODBC, OLEDB and HFSQL engines, where it replaces the host, port and credential fields; replaced by the server otherwise.

authSource.description: Authentication database. Honoured only for MongoDB database types; replaced by the server otherwise.

connType.description: How the connection is expressed. Honoured only for MongoDB database types; for every other engine the value is derived from databaseType and anything sent is replaced.

refreshToken.description: For the GOOGLE BIG QUERY service, the refresh token value.

accessToken.description: For the GOOGLE BIG QUERY service, the access token value.

useSSL.description:
Controls whether the connection is established over SSL.

- **true** - Use this if your database server is set up to serve encrypted data through SSL.
- **false** - Connect without SSL.

useSSLCertificate.description: Whether a client SSL certificate is presented when connecting.

useSSH.description: Whether the connection is tunnelled over SSH. When false, every sshTunnel* attribute is ignored and stored empty.

sshTunnelHost.description: SSH tunnel hostname. Required when useSSH is true.

sshTunnelPort.description: SSH tunnel port. Required when useSSH is true.

sshTunnelUsername.description: SSH tunnel username. Required when useSSH is true.

sshTunnelPassword.description: SSH tunnel password or key passphrase. Required when useSSH is true.

sshTunnelAuthType.description: SSH tunnel authentication method. Read only when useSSH is true.

viewName.description: Name of the table in Zoho Analytics.

viewId.description: ID of the table in Zoho Analytics.

sourceName.description: Name of the corresponding table in the source.

lastSyncTime.description: The time at which the table was last synced.

syncStatus.description: Status of the last sync for this table.

schedule.description: The snapshot's own schedule. Returned for snapshot datasources only.

nextScheduleTime.description: When the snapshot next runs. Returned for snapshot datasources only.

status.description: Whether the snapshot schedule is running. Returned for snapshot datasources only.

SyncIntervals.description: JSONArray with the sync intervals configured for the datasource. Returned when more than one sync interval is configured.

syncIntervalId.description: The unique ID of the sync interval. Send this in the Sync Data CONFIG to sync a specific interval.

lastDataSyncStatus.description: Status of the last data sync for this interval.

lastDataSyncTime.description: The time at which data was last synced for this interval.

schedule.description: The configured sync schedule for this interval.

nextScheduleTime.description: The time at which the next sync is scheduled for this interval.

syncUsed.description: Number of syncs used for this interval.
